A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their readable main text, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–G, and checklists support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across ten LLMs, ablations, mechanism analyses, and additional benchmark, robustness, and utility results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the model comparisons in Tables 1–4 and analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-stage procedure: fine-tuning on refusal answers followed by standard answers to benign questions. No algorithm component, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data, six safety benchmarks in Appendix F.1, GSM8K/MMLU/WritingBench utility tasks, and customization scenario in Appendix G.3. No evaluated coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains AOA, encryption, malicious, indirect malicious, and irrelevant fine-tuning as comparators; appendix comparisons also retain their membership. The new scenario-camouflage citation in G.1 is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The model configurations, fine-tuning settings, HS/DR/ASR evaluation, benchmark sampling, judge-validation procedure, and zero-shot utility protocol are unchanged across the main text and Appendices E–F.

E4.justification: Both retain the AOA variants, stage-1 ablation, system-prompt and LoRA tests, defensive fine-tuning test, loss-landscape and gradient analyses, judge validation, data-randomness tests, and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Appendix F.3 reports averaging three utility-test repetitions in both versions. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars; the checklist's acknowledgment of missing error bars is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including appendix results. Table 1 retains the proposed method's average ASR of 94.84% and HS of 4.48, versus 97.25% and 4.87 for malicious fine-tuning.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 retains the same threat-model assumptions, and Appendix D retains the loss-landscape definition and two-dimensional parameter-slice equation. No mathematical reasoning, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and effectiveness claims: exploiting overfitting with ten benign QA pairs, achieving stealth and high attack success across ten LLMs, and bypassing a token-wise defense.

C2.justification: The overfitting and forgetting explanation, limitations concerning repetitive follow-up responses and hyperparameter dependence, and discussions of defenses and dataset benignness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both provide the same prompts, dataset examples, hyperparameters, hardware and runtime disclosures, alternative-data explanation, and code-access statements. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds scenario camouflage and cites Song et al., Dagger Behind Smile: Fool LLMs with a Happy Ending Story. It also adds an explicit gradient-descent citation to the already-listed Zou et al. work. All 64 earlier references remain; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the affiliation, alphabetizes the bibliography, abbreviates author names, and renumbers citations. Apart from the brief addition in G.1, the prose and section organization remain essentially identical.

P2.justification: Bibliography reformatting changes reference placement and wrapping on pages 10–13, with limited text reflow elsewhere. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4 retain identical displays and captions.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies a small additional related-work example and reformats references, while retaining the same scientific narrative, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations. The modest contextual addition does not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
